contents_summary: One-table Word file (31 text units, all table rows) titled PROCESS CHECKLIST: a title row, a header row (Section, Item, Checklist Description, Page Number) and items 1 to 8b of the case-series reporting guideline with manuscript page numbers. Guideline wording only; no patient data.

units.text: Introduction | 3 | Explain the scientific background and rationale for the case series. What is the unifying theme - common disease, exposure, intervention and outcome, etc. Why is this study needed? | 2
cells: Explain the scientific background and rationale for the case series. What is the unifying theme - common disease, exposure, intervention and outcome, etc. Why is this study needed?

units.text: Methods | 4a | Registration and ethics  State the research registry number in accordance with the declaration of Helsinki - "Every research study involving human subjects must be registered in a publicly accessible database before recruitment of the first subject" (this can be obtained from; ResearchRegistry.com or ClinicalTrials.gov or ISRCTN).  Even retrospective studies should be registered prior to submission. State whether ethical approval was needed and if so, what the relevant judgement reference from the IRB or local ethics committee was? If ethical approval was not needed, state why. | 3
cells:
Registration and ethics 
State the research registry number in accordance with the declaration of Helsinki - "Every research study involving human subjects must be registered in a publicly accessible database before recruitment of the first subject" (this can be obtained from; ResearchRegistry.com or ClinicalTrials.gov or ISRCTN).  Even retrospective studies should be registered prior to submission. State whether ethical approval was needed and if so, what the relevant judgement reference from the IRB or local ethics committee was? If ethical approval was not needed, state why.

units.text: | 4b | Study design  State the study is a case series and whether prospective or retrospective in design, whether single or multi-centre and whether cases are consecutive or non-consecutive. | 3
cells:
Study design 
State the study is a case series and whether prospective or retrospective in design, whether single or multi-centre and whether cases are consecutive or non-consecutive.

units.text: | 4c | Setting Describe the setting(s)and nature of the institution in which the patient was managed; academic, community or private practice setting? Location(s), and relevant dates, including periods of recruitment, exposure, follow-up, and data collection | 3
cells:
Setting
Describe the setting(s)and nature of the institution in which the patient was managed; academic, community or private practice setting? Location(s), and relevant dates, including periods of recruitment, exposure, follow-up, and data collection

units.text: | 4d | Participants Describe the relevant characteristics of the participants (comorbidities, tumour staging, smoking status, etc). State any eligibility (inclusion/exclusion) criteria and the sources and methods of selection of participants. Describe length and methods of follow-up. | 3
cells:
Participants
Describe the relevant characteristics of the participants (comorbidities, tumour staging, smoking status, etc). State any eligibility (inclusion/exclusion) criteria and the sources and methods of selection of participants. Describe length and methods of follow-up.

units.text: | 4e | Pre-intervention considerations  e.g. Patient optimisation: measures taken prior to surgery or other intervention e.g. treating hypothermia/hypovolaemia/hypotension in burns patients, ICU care for sepsis, dealing with anticoagulation/other medications and so on. | 3
cells:
Pre-intervention considerations
 e.g. Patient optimisation: measures taken prior to surgery or other intervention e.g. treating hypothermia/hypovolaemia/hypotension in burns patients, ICU care for sepsis, dealing with anticoagulation/other medications and so on.

units.text: | 4f | Types of intervention(s) deployed  To include reasoning behind treatment offered (pharmacological, surgical, physiotherapy, psychological, preventive) and concurrent treatments (antibiotics, analgesia, anti-emetics, nil by mouth, VTE prophylaxis, etc). Medical devices should have manufacturer and model specifically mentioned. | 3
cells:
Types of intervention(s) deployed 
To include reasoning behind treatment offered (pharmacological, surgical, physiotherapy, psychological, preventive) and concurrent treatments (antibiotics, analgesia, anti-emetics, nil by mouth, VTE prophylaxis, etc). Medical devices should have manufacturer and model specifically mentioned.

units.text: | 4g | Peri-intervention considerations Administration of intervention (what, where, when and how was it done, including details for surgery; anaesthesia, patient position, use of tourniquet and other relevant equipment, preparation used, sutures, devices, surgical stage (1 or 2 stage, etc) and operative time. Pharmacological therapies should include formulation, dosage, strength, route and duration).  Authors are encouraged to use figures, diagrams, photos, video and other multimedia to explain their intervention. | 3
cells:
Peri-intervention considerations
Administration of intervention (what, where, when and how was it done, including details for surgery; anaesthesia, patient position, use of tourniquet and other relevant equipment, preparation used, sutures, devices, surgical stage (1 or 2 stage, etc) and operative time. Pharmacological therapies should include formulation, dosage, strength, route and duration).  Authors are encouraged to use figures, diagrams, photos, video and other multimedia to explain their intervention.

units.text: | 4h | Who performed the procedure(s)  Operator experience (position on the learning curve for the technique if established, specialisation and prior relevant training). | 3
cells:
Who performed the procedure(s) 
Operator experience (position on the learning curve for the technique if established, specialisation and prior relevant training).

units.text: | 4i | Quality control  What measures were taken to reduce inter or intra-operator variation. What measures were taken to ensure quality and consistency in the delivery of the intervention e.g. independent observers, lymph node counts, etc | 3
cells:
Quality control 
What measures were taken to reduce inter or intra-operator variation. What measures were taken to ensure quality and consistency in the delivery of the intervention e.g. independent observers, lymph node counts, etc

units.text: | 4j | Post-intervention considerations  e.g. post-operative instructions and place of care. Important follow-up measures - diagnostic and other test results. Future surveillance requirements - e.g. imaging surveillance of endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) or clinical exam/ultrasound of regional lymph nodes for skin cancer. | 3
cells:
Post-intervention considerations 
e.g. post-operative instructions and place of care. Important follow-up measures - diagnostic and other test results. Future surveillance requirements - e.g. imaging surveillance of endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) or clinical exam/ultrasound of regional lymph nodes for skin cancer.

units.text: Results | 5a | Participants Report numbers involved and their characteristics (co-morbidities, tumour staging, smoking status, etc). | 3
cells:
Participants
Report numbers involved and their characteristics (co-morbidities, tumour staging, smoking status, etc).

units.text: | 5b | Changes Any changes in the interventions during the course of the case series (how has it evolved, been altered or tinkered with, what learning occurred, etc) together with rationale and a diagram if appropriate. Degree of novelty for a surgical technique/device should be mentioned and a comment on learning curves should be made for new techniques/devices. | 3
cells:
Changes
Any changes in the interventions during the course of the case series (how has it evolved, been altered or tinkered with, what learning occurred, etc) together with rationale and a diagram if appropriate. Degree of novelty for a surgical technique/device should be mentioned and a comment on learning curves should be made for new techniques/devices.

units.text: | 5c | Outcomes and follow-up  Clinician assessed and patient-reported outcomes (when appropriate) should be stated with inclusion of the time periods at which assessed. Relevant photographs/radiological images should be provided e.g. 12-month follow-up. | 3
cells:
Outcomes and follow-up 
Clinician assessed and patient-reported outcomes (when appropriate) should be stated with inclusion of the time periods at which assessed. Relevant photographs/radiological images should be provided e.g. 12-month follow-up.

units.text: | 5d | Intervention adherence/compliance and tolerability   How was this assessed. Describe loss to follow-up (express as a percentage and a fraction) and any explanations for it. | 3
cells:
Intervention adherence/compliance and tolerability 
 How was this assessed. Describe loss to follow-up (express as a percentage and a fraction) and any explanations for it.

units.text: | 5e | Complications and adverse or unanticipated events Described in detail and ideally categorised in accordance with the Clavien-Dindo Classification. How they were prevented, mitigated, diagnosed and managed. Blood loss, wound complications, re-exploration/revision surgery, 30-day post-op and long-term morbidity/mortality may need to be specified. | 3
